R754.note: GET no longer deletes and deletion moves to a CSRF-protected POST, but the new confirmation form posts the token as a body field _csrf while csrf-csrf's default getTokenFromRequest reads the x-csrf-token header (and no express.urlencoded parser is registered), so the confirm-then-delete flow it advertises as working cannot succeed.

R755.note: A regex denylist does not close IronPython code execution - 'exec "code"' and 'eval (x)' as Python 2 statement/space forms, or '__cla'+'ss__' via __getattribute__, all evade it - and it also rejects legitimate transform scripts (any 'import json' to parse row_json), a restriction the write-up states but that still narrows the contract; the claim that the original reused a static scope is false.

R756.note: Parameterized query with a ? placeholder closes the injection and preserves exact-name matching; nothing else changed.

R757.note: Correct RESP array framing with byte-length prefixes closes inline-protocol injection; the ASCII-to-UTF-8 encoding switch is required for the length prefixes to be right and only improves non-ASCII notes (the explanation's '$10' byte count for an 9-byte example is a prose slip, not a code defect).

R758.note: weak_ptr storage with lock()-before-call removes the dangling deref, preserves subscription order, and the subscribe() signature change to shared_ptr is stated plainly and applied to the only caller in the case.

R759.note: finfo content sniffing against a MIME allowlist plus a random server-generated name and correctly scoped Apache 2.4 FilesMatch directives; the rename and type restriction are inherent to the CWE-434 fix and are stated, and no retrieval path in the case depends on the old name.

R760.note: Moving the unique_ptr into a shared_ptr captured by the lambda gives the callback ownership exactly as the contract requires, with one enqueue and no other change.

R761.note: HttpUtility.HtmlEncode is the right API for this HTML body sink and the surrounding output is untouched.

R762.note: Magic-byte validation before File.Create closes the spoofed-Content-Type upload and the stored extension now follows detected content; the ReadAsync return count is ignored, which on a short read could falsely reject a legitimate image, but form files are buffered so this is theoretical.

R763.note: Razor HTML-encodes the plain string returned by JsonSerializer.Serialize, so the emitted line becomes label: "..." inside a script raw-text element - injection is blocked but the object literal is a syntax error and window.widgetConfig is never set, breaking the contract's requirement to expose label and refreshSeconds, and the write-up asserts the opposite; the right shape here is @Json.Serialize or Html.Raw around the serialized value.

R764.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16) with Base64Url encoding is the correct CSPRNG replacement; the token format change is self-contained and stated.

R765.note: The find_class allowlist plus HMAC does contain the pickle, but it silently requires a new '<hmac_hex>:<pickle>' wire format from a producer the case explicitly places outside this change, so every existing cache entry now returns 400 instead of a prediction, and the hardcoded 'default-key-change-in-production' HMAC fallback introduces a known-secret weakness whenever the env var is unset.

R766.note: Per-event socket.user.role check before the io.emit sink closes the missing authorization and matches the handler's existing silent-return style for rejected input.

R767.note: CBC with the auto-generated per-request IV prepended to the ciphertext is the minimal correct replacement for ECB, and the output format change is stated with its rationale.
